Test Performed: Compared HR termination list (Q1-Q2) to active Okta user accounts
Finding: 14 terminated employees retained active Okta accounts 30+ days after offboarding date; one account active 87 days post-termination
Root Cause: HR-to-IT ticket process has no automated trigger; deprovisioning relies on manual submission of offboarding ticket
Recommendation: Integrate HRIS with Okta provisioning via SCIM; automate deprovisioning within 24 hours of termination event; implement daily reconciliation report between HR and IT

Test Performed: Reviewed privileged accounts against defined role matrix
Finding: 3 of 25 privileged users reviewed had access beyond their defined role - all three granted elevated access for a specific project and never revoked after completion
Root Cause: Access was granted on an ad hoc basis for project delivery; no formal access recertification or role reassessment process exists
Recommendation: Implement quarterly PAM access recertification via automated access review workflow; require written re-approval for all elevated roles every 90 days

Test Performed: Reviewed Okta admin console for MFA enrollment status across all account types
Finding: MFA not enabled on 6 of 18 service accounts with direct production system access (AWS RDS Snowflake GitHub API) - Critical SOC 2 finding
Root Cause: Service accounts were explicitly excluded from MFA policy during initial Okta configuration; no documented risk acceptance exists for this exception
Recommendation: Enforce MFA or certificate-based authentication on all service accounts immediately; no exceptions without formal risk acceptance signed by CISO; implement machine identity management (CyberArk or AWS IAM Roles)

Test Performed: Reviewed Okta last-login timestamps for all active accounts
Finding: 8 of 40 accounts reviewed had no login activity in 90+ days; 3 belonged to contractors whose engagements had ended with no offboarding ticket filed
Root Cause: No automated dormant account detection process exists; Okta reports require manual export and analysis
Recommendation: Implement automated dormant account review using Okta Workflows or AWS Lambda; automatically disable accounts inactive for 60+ days; require reactivation approval

Test Performed: Reviewed database access credentials for all production RDS instances
Finding: One shared administrative account dbadmin_shared was actively used by 3 engineers for production database access; individual privileged accounts had not been provisioned for database-level access
Root Cause: Shared credentials established during initial database setup for convenience; individual provisioning process not followed due to perceived overhead
Recommendation: Immediately eliminate shared accounts; provision individual privileged database accounts for each engineer; implement session recording (AWS Systems Manager Session Manager or CyberArk); rotate shared credentials immediately
